title: Utilizing Sparsity in the GPU-accelerated Assembly of Schur Complement Matrices in Domain Decomposition Methods
problem: Domain decomposition methods compute Schur complement matrices for solving large engineering problems on HPC systems. GPU assembly of explicit dense Schur complements incurs significant overhead, adding overhead to GPU acceleration benefits.
motivation: Domain decomposition methods scale well on supercomputers but require expensive explicit Schur complement assembly on GPUs. Previous work showed GPU assembly reduces overhead, but potential to further optimize by exploiting matrix sparsity patterns has been unexplored.
method: GPU-accelerated Schur complement assembly exploiting matrix sparsity: (1) Direct GPU assembly avoiding host-side overhead, (2) Wisely utilize sparsity patterns to reduce memory and computation, (3) Applied to FETI (Finite Element Tearing and Interconnecting) method.
key_novelty: First systematic exploitation of matrix sparsity in GPU-accelerated Schur complement assembly, achieving significant speedup over dense assembly approach.
contributions: Sparsity-aware GPU assembly algorithm for Schur complement matrices
5.1x speedup in GPU computation section, 3.3x overall assembly speedup
Reduced overhead making GPU acceleration beneficial from 10+ iterations
Application to FETI with subdomains of 1,000-70,000 unknowns
limitations: Abstract-only; specific sparsity patterns, algorithm details, and applicability to other domain decomposition methods not provided.
primary_theme: Sparsity-aware GPU kernels for domain decomposition
